mentl/4db8f76:
ROOT-CAUSE FIX (the corruption that's been blocking L1 closure):

Output buffer was at 16 MiB — INSIDE perm arena's 1-1537 MiB range.
On wheel-scale compiles, perm grew past 16 MiB and overwrote the
buffer's address range AND adjacent perm-allocated state (funcref
ledger entries, fn-name strings, list nodes). The corruption
manifested as:
  - wat2wasm errors at line 23 (or wherever the corruption first
    surfaced as invalid WAT structure)
  - duplicate (table)/(elem)/(global)/etc. sections
  - structural body corruption mid-file
  - the closure-capture dedup intermittently failing as funcref
    entries got overwritten

Fix: extend memory by 8 MiB (32768 → 32896 pages) and move $out_base
to 2 GiB (post-fn arena's 2048 MiB cap). Output buffer is now in a
disjoint region that perm cannot reach. Substrate-honest arena
discipline instead of probabilistic non-collision.

CONSOLIDATION (drift 7 closure):

With the corruption gone, the previously-attempted deep consolidation
becomes safe:
  - Delete $collect_fn_names + $cfn_walk + $cfn_walk_list (~150 lines).
    The funcref ledger ($emit_funcref_table_ptr) is populated by
    $emit_fn_body via $emit_funcref_register_first as the actual emit
    walk runs — single source of truth.
  - Delete $emit_funcref_section (subsumed by $emit_fn_table_and_globals).
  - Delete $emit_find_name_index (replaced by $emit_funcref_lookup at
    its only consumer, $emit_static_top_closures).
  - Reorder $mentl_emit: $emit_functions runs FIRST (populates funcref);
    $emit_fn_table_and_globals + $emit_static_top_closures iterate the
    funcref ledger directly.
  - Update $emit_fn_table_and_globals signature: drop $names param.
  - Update $emit_static_top_closures signature: drop $all_names param.
  - Drop $fn_names local from $mentl_emit.

mentl/4d0fce1:
The most beneficial substrate move available per the kernel-closure
milestone (insight #13). 17 of 22 Interact arms are substrate-live but
no transport surfaces them; lsp_adapter is the bridge that makes
Mentl SPEAK to a real editor (VS Code via the LSP plugin path).

Per MV walkthrough §1.5: Interact is the stable API boundary; LSP is
one transport over it. Per Insight #11 (Continuous Oracle IS IC +
cached value): lsp_adapter is the first real subscriber that closes
the realization loop in editor-time. Per Insight #1 (handler chain
IS capability stack): lsp_adapter sits OUTERMOST — least trusted,
sandbox boundary.

Designs three substrate layers:

Layer A — JSON-RPC framing (Content-Length headers + length-prefixed
bodies). Two fns: read_lsp_frame / write_lsp_frame on Memory + WASI.

Layer B — JSON parse/serialize (JsonValue ADT + recursive descent
parser + canonical serializer). Reusable substrate beyond LSP — web
playground, MCP, debug adapter all compose on it. Lands as MV-LSP.json
peer sub-handle (separate commit).

Layer C — lsp_adapter handler + session loop. Reads stdin frame loop;
classifies LSP method strings to LspMethodKind ADT (per drift mode 8
prevention: string IS input, immediately projected to ADT; downstream
dispatch matches ADT only); dispatches to handle_* fns; each handle_*
performs Interact ops + projects to LspResponseBody.

Routing table (12 v1 LSP methods → 14 Interact ops):
  initialize / initialized / shutdown / exit  — server lifecycle
  textDocument/didOpen     → open_file
  textDocument/didChange   → edit (gates on MV.2.e.P.edit)
  textDocument/didSave     → save_file
  textDocument/didClose    → close_file (FX.5)
  textDocument/hover       → focus + ask(QTypeAt)
  textDocument/completion  → propose
  textDocument/codeAction  → propose
  textDocument/diagnostic  → run_check (gates on Run.run_check)
  textDocument/definition  → focus + ask(QWhy)
  textDocument/references  → focus + ask(QRefsOf)

After full MV-LSP arc lands: 8 of 10 MV.2.

two-top/4d9a984:
Lands the rest of the input layer: quantization at the wire boundary,
the rolled-back input ring that feeds edge detection and forgiveness,
and an on-screen debug readout for tuning. With this cycle the touch
state actually flows through GGRS into sim — `DefaultInputsPlugin` is
gone from the app and `TouchInputsPlugin` takes its place.

Cycle 5 — TouchInputsPlugin + app swap:
  * crates/input_touch/Cargo.toml: pulls in bevy_ggrs = "=0.21" and
    sim (path) so the read-inputs system can write LocalInputs<GgrsCfg>.
  * input_touch::quantize_angle: pure helper, [-π, π] → u8 covering one
    full turn. Floor + clamp; π wraps to 255 (just below) and -π lands
    on 0 so the byte space is cyclic without overflow.
  * input_touch::quantize_inputs: pure helper, TouchState → 4-byte
    PlayerInput. Stick scaled to i8 in [-127, 127]. stick_y is negated
    here because Bevy reports y-down screen coords but the wire format
    follows game-space (y-up) so sim can use stick_y as a velocity
    multiplier directly. Buttons are THROW_DOWN (= throw_held) and
    AIM_ACTIVE (= aim_active); aim_angle is 0 when not active so the
    wire byte stays clean.
  * input_touch::read_local_touch_inputs: ReadInputs system, mirrors
    the shape of sim::read_local_inputs — same map-into-LocalInputs
    pattern but reads from TouchState instead of SynthesizedInputs.
  * input_touch::TouchInputsPlugin: production input source. Adds
    InputTouchPlugin (the PreUpdate touch pipeline from cycles 1-4)
    plus the ReadInputs hookup. Mutually exclusive with
    DefaultInputsPlugin — the two would race over LocalInputs.
  * crates/app/src/lib.rs: TouchInputsPlugin replaces
    DefaultInputsPlugin; drive_inputs (oscillating SynthesizedInputs)
    is gone; new update_window_metrics system in PreUpdate (ordered
    .before(input_touch::update_touch_state)) populates WindowSize
    and CursorPosition each frame from the primary Window.
    update_window_metrics lives in app rather than input_touch so
perennials/4d59be7:
The comments ran one em dash every 57 words and the UI copy eight in
519. Hand-written prose in this house runs about one pair per 5,600
words; the dash-heavy voice was never Morgan's, it was the machine's.
Each of the 150 is replaced by the punctuation the sentence actually
wanted: a period where there were two beats, a semicolon where the
clauses lean on each other, a colon where the second half expands the
first, parentheses where the dash pair was a true aside. Nothing is
substituted mechanically, which is the point; one of them turned out
to be a real parenthetical whose clause a period would have orphaned.

The visible copy changes with it: "Tap the sheet to place. Tap again
for a drift." The one surviving dash quotes what the omnibox used to
render, so it stays a quote. The notebook export takes the app's own ·
separator in its header. Down to one dash in 8,192 words of comment,
and none in the copy.
